subject: Request: KMS/HSM log delivery plan and redaction for CAIQ/SIG
messages:
From: Alyssa Wei <alyssa.wei@valora-analytics.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 12 Sep 2028 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: KMS artifacts for CAIQ/SIG - what you can provide

Hi Irene,

Thanks for taking this on. Valora's security team is finalizing the CAIQ/SIG packet and we have a couple of focused asks on your KMS/HSM controls so we can close the section on Key Management and Cryptography. Specifically: 

- A short extract (CSV or JSON) showing key rotation events for the last 90 days (key id, rotated_at, operator_id, rotation_type - scheduled/emergency) with any sensitive identifiers redacted.
- HSM attestation/certificate for the device that stores tenant KEKs (we can accept vendor-signed PDFs).
- A brief note describing the emergency rotate playbook and the average detection-to-rotation time in the past year.

Can you confirm what format you can provide, any PII we should remove, and the preferred transfer method? Our compliance team requires a hashed identifier for keys rather than raw key IDs.

Best,
Alyssa

--
Alyssa Wei
Senior InfoSec Analyst, Valora Analytics
alyssa.wei@valora-analytics.com
From: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>
To: Alyssa Wei <alyssa.wei@valora-analytics.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 12 Sep 2028 12:08:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: KMS artifacts for CAIQ/SIG - what you can provide

Hi Alyssa,

Thanks — we can provide the items you listed. Quick summary of what Redwood can deliver and how: 

1) Rotation extract: CSV (sample attached) containing columns: hashed_key_id, rotated_at (ISO8601), rotation_reason (scheduled|emergency|rekey), operator (redacted to role: "sysadmin" / "ops-rotation-bot"), and rotation_request_ticket (internal id masked). We will mask tenant IDs and only provide hashed_key_id using SHA256(prefix + key_uuid) so it is consistent but non-reversible.

2) HSM Attestation: vendor-signed PDF (attached: hsm_attestation-2028-08.pdf). It includes firmware & module identifiers and certificate chain. Note that we keep full HSM serials off external packets; the attestation contains the minimum proof-of-seal most auditors accept.

3) Emergency rotate/playbook: short narrative + SLAs. For the last 12 months our median detection-to-rotation for high-impact keys is ~45 minutes after confirmed compromise; emergency rotates are triggered by SecOps and executed via our orchestration runbook. We'll include the redacted runbook excerpt.

Delivery preferences: SFTP to an allowlisted Valora host (we can push a GPG-encrypted tarball) or a short-term authenticated Drive share. Please confirm which you prefer.

I'll loop Marissa to coordinate the redaction checklist and provide the CSV sample.

Thanks,
Irene

--
Irene Choi
Staff Security Engineer, Redwood Inference
irene.choi@redwood.com
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>, Alyssa Wei <alyssa.wei@valora-analytics.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 13 Sep 2028 08:46:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: KMS artifacts for CAIQ/SIG - what you can provide

Hi all,

Attached is a redacted sample rotation extract: redacted_kms_rotation_sample.csv (columns described below). A couple of notes on redaction rules we applied: 

- raw key UUIDs replaced with hashed_key_id using the prefix method Irene mentioned.
- operator field generalized to role labels (no personal emails or usernames).
- rotation_request_ticket masked to a short numeric token tied to our internal ticketing system (we will provide mapping under NDA if required).
- no tenant or customer PII included.

We are also including a short markdown doc (redaction_guidelines.md) that describes how we handle masking and an anonymized example of an emergency rotate timeline.

If Valora needs unredacted logs for an auditor, we can arrange an in-person or NDAed remote review session where the auditor can verify raw artifacts without retention. For CAIQ/SIG, this redacted slice is usually sufficient.

Preferred transfer: GPG-encrypted tarball to your SFTP host. Please provide the host + user and a public key, or we can generate one and send the pubkey.

Marissa

--
Marissa Cole
Compliance Program Manager, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com
From: Alyssa Wei <alyssa.wei@valora-analytics.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 14 Sep 2028 10:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: KMS artifacts for CAIQ/SIG - what you can provide

Thanks Marissa — this is helpful. A few clarifying items from Valora Security: 

1) Please include a checksum (SHA256) of the CSV extract in the transfer manifest so our ingest can verify integrity.
2) For the emergency rotate timeline, can you include one redacted example event showing detection timestamp, decision timestamp, and completion timestamp (relative ordering only) for audit sampling?
3) We'll accept SFTP + GPG as long as you also provide the public key we should expect; please send the host/user and key by 9/15 close of business.

If you can provide those, we can mark the CAIQ 'Cryptography' section as addressed and proceed to the SIG download.

Best,
Alyssa

--
Alyssa Wei
Senior InfoSec Analyst, Valora Analytics
From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
To: Alyssa Wei <alyssa.wei@valora-analytics.com>
Cc: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 15 Sep 2028 11:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: KMS artifacts for CAIQ/SIG - what you can provide

Hi Alyssa — sending host details and pubkey below. We will push the GPG-encrypted tarball containing: redacted_kms_rotation_sample.csv, redaction_guidelines.md, and hsm_attestation-2028-08.pdf. Additionally, included in the tarball is a single redacted emergency event example (timestamps are in UTC):

- detection_ts: 2028-05-02T03:21:00Z
- decision_ts: 2028-05-02T03:28:00Z
- completion_ts: 2028-05-02T04:05:00Z
